use_case_summary: Customer support SaaS building real-time agent assist: streaming token-level suggestions in agent UI, automatic ticket summarization after call, and safe tool-calling into Zendesk/CRM. Must maintain p95/p99 latency SLOs during spikes, support automatic fallback to cheaper model variants, and provide strong guardrails for hallucination and PII redaction.
notes:
- Primary product: live agent UI that overlays streaming suggestions and canned responses.
- Key metric: p99 infer latency target <= 150ms for suggestions, p95 < 80ms for short prompts.
- Concurrency profile: 2k concurrent agents during peak promo events; burst to 6k for 10-30 min windows.
- Concern: current vendor misses spikes; agents see slow suggestion lag.
- Security: must pass SOC2 questionnaire, SSO/SAML, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, customer-managed KMS for keys. Data residency required for EU customers.
- Integration: tool-calling webhook flows to Zendesk, internal orchestration service; want Redwood to support function/tool-calling and structured outputs for downstream automation.
- Guardrails requested: hallucination-detection heuristic, confidence score per suggestion, deny-listing of PII fields, and automatic human-handoff trigger when confidence < 0.4.
- POC scope: 48-hour soak on Dedicated, synthetic spike generator (provided by AidStream), 1000 concurrent simulated agents then ramp to 6k. Measure latency SLOs, token cost, and fallback success rate.
- Quote from CTO (paraphrase): "We need streaming suggestions that feel instant — agents can't wait. If Redwood can prove p99 under spikes, procurement moves fast."
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (Marta Reyes), VP Product (Arjun Patel), Head of Ops (Lena Morris).
- Next: Send POC kick-off checklist, finalize SOC2 addendum, set dates for 48-hour run (requested start 2026-04-15).
